subject: Pacify Health: access evidence & SCIM/RBAC artifacts for SIG/CAIQ
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@pacifyhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: security+evidence@pacifyhealth.com
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — access controls evidence needed

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is preparing the SIG and CAIQ pack and we need a focused set of artifacts to close the Access Control (IAM) section. Can you help with the following items by EOD Wednesday?

- SCIM delta export covering March 1–20, 2027 (CSV)
- Sample SAML assertion (anonymized) for a successful login path
- Current RBAC matrix (roles → privileges) and the owner for each role
- Evidence of least-privilege enforcement for service accounts (rotation policy or exception log)

If any of these require an NDA or separate transfer method, let me know. We can accept a Drive link or SFTP drop.

Regards,
Claire Thompson
Security Engineer | Pacify Health

--
Note: security+evidence@pacifyhealth.com is monitoring this request for SOC/SIG intake.

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@pacifyhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — access controls evidence needed

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear checklist. Looping in Jonas (infrastructure lead) and Ben (customer security liaison) to coordinate artifact delivery. Quick notes:

- We can produce a SCIM delta export and an access matrix; I expect the CSV + XLSX will cover the first three bullets.
- SAML assertion samples: we will sanitize PII and show the assertion headers and attribute mappings.
- Service accounts: Jonas will pull the rotation/exception logs; we may redact keys but provide the policy doc and the rotation events.

Jonas/Ben — can you confirm earliest time for a sanitized SCIM delta and an RBAC matrix? Claire asked for EOD Wednesday (3/24). If that's tight, propose next-day delivery with interim artifacts.

Mina Haddad
Head of Partner Security Operations

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up — access controls evidence needed

Claire / Mina — attaching the initial artifact bundle for review. Attachments: scim-delta-snapshot-20270321.csv, access-matrix-pacify-20270322.xlsx, sso-assertions-sample.txt (sanitized).

Delivery notes:
- SCIM export: includes create/update/delete events with timestamps and actor (anonymized user ids). We excluded password fields and any tenant-specific PII.
- RBAC matrix: current roles are columned with privilege sets; the rightmost column lists the recorded owner (team or individual alias).
- SAML assertion: sample contains typical NameID, audience, and role attributes; timestamps preserved, unique identifiers redacted.

Open items we still need to pull:
1) Service account rotation events (we have rotation metadata but need to redact service principal ids)
2) Any historical exception approvals for elevated service account privileges — we have a 2026–2027 exceptions ledger in Jira (link below).

Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

- RBAC matrix is XLSX with drop-down role descriptions and an owner column. I’ll export a flattened CSV version if that helps your tooling.

- Service account rotation: we have the rotation events in our secrets manager audit logs; due to sensitivity we will provide a summarized CSV of rotation timestamps and policy references rather than raw secret identifiers.

Team — received the Drive link and the SCIM CSV; thank you for the quick turnaround. A couple follow-ups after my initial pass:

- Can you provide a short README that maps the CSV columns to your internal event types (create/update/delete) and the anonymization approach used? That helps our ingest and auditors.
- We noticed one service account entry in the access matrix marked as "legacy-service-account" with owner "infra-admins" — could you provide the exception approval and the last rotation timestamp for that account? If rotation happened before Jan 2027, we need an upgrade plan.

If you can drop those two items by EOD Friday, that should close the access control section. Appreciate your help — Claire

Claire Thompson
